actions.title: Challenging Determinism in Value Formation

assumptions: Memory ingestion is the primary driver of agent preference formation.
Non-deterministic environmental inputs can be introduced without affecting the agent's core processing logic.
definition.falsification: If the preference outcomes for all agents remain identical across 100 randomized input sequences, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: If environmental input sequences are randomized using a non-deterministic process, agents with identical initialization will produce statistically significant divergence in preference outcomes, falsifying the assumption of outcome determinism.
definition.uncertainty: The specific threshold for 'significant divergence' is hypothesized and requires validation via the experimental protocol.
